activity_409.observed: the first POST .../activity returned 409 Conflict, later POSTs returned 200
activity_409.cause: the StrictMode first-mount cleanup flushes the logger before the queue response sets candidate_set_hash, so the batch is sent with an empty hash and the server rejects a mismatched bundle
activity_409.impact: none — makeActivityLogger keeps an unacknowledged batch in localStorage and resends it with the same event_id; the rejected events (session_started, queue_load_started) are present in the stored activity log
activity_409.dev_only: StrictMode double-mount does not happen in a production build; not treated as a bug

findings.title: class_name is null for every candidate, so the judging question reads '이 객체 라벨이…' instead of '이 Car 라벨이…'
findings.where: upstream — label_diagnosis.aida_v2_candidate_iou.json review_queue rows already carry class_name: null; the snapshot and the queue simply pass it through
findings.impact: the dataset is single-class (classes.txt = Car), so nothing is ambiguous, but the class name is not actually visible on the judging screen even though the design lists it as a visible field
findings.action: not fixed — the cause is in diagnosis output, not in the rendering; changing it is a data/behaviour decision for the user

findings.title: the browser judging screen shows the crop only; there is no full-scene view
findings.where: AdjudicationView renders one 340x340 crop centred on the candidate box, with other labels drawn in blue
findings.impact: handoff item 4 asks to check both the full scene and the crop; the full-scene file exists only for the AI adjudicator manifest (full_file), not for the human screen. Other labels visible inside the crop are drawn, so nearby context is partly covered, but objects outside the crop are not.
findings.action: not fixed — design decision, reported for the user

findings.detail: see d_console_and_network.activity_409 — self-healing, no data loss, StrictMode-only
